description: A single upstream dependency state change that affects delivery for one or more packages within a media buy. An impairment is open until the underlying resource returns to a serviceable state. Materiality: an impairment MUST list at least one package whose ability to serve is degraded; cosmetic-only effects (e.g., one rejected creative when peers remain serviceable in the same package) MUST NOT be reported as impairments. Sellers MAY report conservatively when uncertain (list a package when the materiality join is expensive to compute); sellers MUST NOT report when serving is provably unaffected. Materiality is required (MUST) for resource types where the resource→buy join is cheap and 1:N — audience, event_source, property; SHOULD-strength for creative and catalog_item, where the resource is shared across a larger pool and the join cost is higher.

impairment_id.description: Stable identifier for this impairment, used as the notification_id when the impairment fires via webhook. Stable across re-emissions of the same open impairment (e.g., the seller re-fires after the buyer's receiver was down) and across the closing fire that signals resolution. A new impairment for the same resource_id after closure receives a new impairment_id. Distinct from the per-fire idempotency_key issued at the webhook transport layer — see snapshot-and-log Rule 1. Receivers correlate webhook fires to current impairments[] state by impairment_id; receivers suppress duplicate transport-layer retries by idempotency_key. Seeing the same impairment_id with different idempotency_keys is a re-emission signal, not a retry — the buyer should treat it as a notice that something may have been missed.

observed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the seller observed the resource transition to its offline state.

package_ids.description: Packages within this media buy whose delivery is degraded by the impairment. MUST list at least one package — cosmetic effects that do not degrade any package's ability to serve MUST NOT be reported as impairments.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation. Supplements reason_code with seller-specific detail.

reason_code.description: Categorical reason for the offline transition. Drives buyer-side remediation logic.

enumDescriptions.consent_expired: Consent basis for using the resource has lapsed (e.g., hashed identifier consent expiry on a synced audience). Applies to: audience.
enumDescriptions.content_rejected: Previously-approved creative content was re-reviewed and rejected. Applies to: creative.
enumDescriptions.identity_authorization_expired: Authorization for a creative's referenced identity or post expired. Applies to: creative, especially `published_post` reference creatives. Offline state is usually `suspended` while authorization can be renewed.
enumDescriptions.identity_authorization_revoked: Authorization for a creative's referenced identity or post was revoked. Applies to: creative, especially `published_post` reference creatives. Offline state is usually `suspended` while authorization can be restored.
enumDescriptions.pii_audit_failed: Resource failed a privacy / PII audit. Applies to: audience.
enumDescriptions.policy_violation: Seller policy enforcement removed the resource from active use. Applies to: audience, creative, catalog_item, property.
enumDescriptions.property_depublished: Property was depublished or removed from the seller's catalog via brand.json / adagents.json. Verification is via the publisher's brand.json / adagents.json files. Applies to: property.
enumDescriptions.seller_removed: Seller withdrew the resource from active use for operational reasons not covered by other codes (e.g., inventory withdrawal). Applies to: catalog_item, audience, creative, property. Distinct from policy_violation (seller-policy-driven) and from catalog_item's withdrawn state (the lifecycle endpoint) — this code is the impairment reason that surfaces when a previously-active resource is withdrawn.
enumDescriptions.source_offline: Underlying event/signal source stopped firing (zero events received over the seller's evaluation window). Applies to: event_source.
enumDescriptions.source_private: A creative's referenced source post became private or inaccessible to the seller. Applies to: creative, especially `published_post` reference creatives. Offline state is usually `suspended` while visibility can be restored.
enumDescriptions.ttl_expired: Resource exceeded its time-to-live and was retired by the seller. Applies to: audience.

reason_code.title: Impairment Reason Code

remediation.description: Action the buyer can take to clear the impairment, if any. Free text. Absent when no buyer-side remediation is possible (e.g., seller-initiated withdrawal pending re-publication).

resource_id.description: Seller's identifier for the specific resource that transitioned. References the same id space as the corresponding sync_/list_ task responses (e.g., audience_id, creative_id).

resource_type.description: The kind of upstream dependency that transitioned to an offline state. Values are drawn from the x-entity vocabulary (see core/x-entity-types.json) and identify a buyer-referenced object with its own lifecycle that the seller can take offline. This is the subset of x-entity types for which a media buy's serving depends on the resource — not a new typology, just the impairment-relevant slice.

transition.description: The resource-level status transition that triggered this impairment.

from.description: Prior status of the resource (e.g., 'ready', 'approved', 'good'). Optional — sellers SHOULD include when known, MAY omit when the resource was discovered already in an offline state (e.g., a property depublished via brand.json crawl with no prior snapshot). Open string at the schema layer because each resource_type has its own serviceable-state vocabulary; the pattern constraint blocks free-form garbage, and the impairment.coherence assertion validates that 'from' is a known serviceable value for the resource_type.

to.description: Current (offline) status of the resource. Drawn from the resource_type's canonical lifecycle enum; see impairment-offline-state for per-value resource_type pairing. The pairing is validated by impairment.coherence.

enumDescriptions.depublished: Synthetic offline marker — property has no per-resource status field; publication state is derived from brand.json / adagents.json. Valid when resource_type='property'.
enumDescriptions.insufficient: Offline value of assessment-status surfaced through event-source-health.status. Valid when resource_type='event_source'. Covers source-offline (zero events received over the evaluation window) — disambiguate via events_received_24h and last_event_at.
enumDescriptions.rejected: Offline value of creative-status. Valid when resource_type='creative'. Reached from approved when seller revokes post-approval.
enumDescriptions.suspended: Offline value of audience-status and a recoverable offline value of creative-status. Valid when resource_type='audience', and valid when resource_type='creative' for recoverable dependency/authorization loss such as a published-post authorization expiring or a source post becoming private.
enumDescriptions.withdrawn: Offline value of catalog-item-status. Valid when resource_type='catalog_item'. Seller-initiated removal, distinct from review-failure rejection.

to.title: Impairment Offline State

title: Impairment
